name: Mercado de Campo de Ourique
seoTitle: Mercado de Campo de Ourique: A Local Lunch Off Tram 28
tagline: A 1934 neighbourhood market with a food hall, worth the trip only if you want a local lunch at the end of tram 28

description.short: A municipal market in the residential Campo de Ourique district, opened in 1934 and remodelled in 2013 with food counters and shared tables in the central hall. Fresh-food stalls trade alongside. About 4.2 km from the cruise terminal.
description.full:
Most cruise passengers will not need to come here. It is a neighbourhood market about 4.2 km west of the ship, with no sights of its own, and the Time Out Market at Cais do Sodré is closer if all you want is a food hall. Campo de Ourique suits a different visitor: someone on a second or third trip to Lisbon, someone who wants lunch among residents rather than tour groups, or someone riding tram 28 to the end of the line who needs a reason to get off.

To get there, take a taxi (about 15 minutes), or ride tram 28 to its western terminus at Campo de Ourique (Prazeres) and walk a few minutes into the district. Tram 28 is slow and often full; from the terminal you can board it in Alfama, but expect to stand or wait for a second car in high season.

The market has two parts. The traditional stalls sell fish, meat, fruit and vegetables, bacalhau, bread, charcuterie, tinned fish, spices and flowers, and are busiest and best stocked in the morning. The central hall holds food and drink counters with shared tables; locals fill it at lunch from about 12:30 and again in the evening. The building is open from 07:00 every day, until 23:00 from Sunday to Wednesday and until 01:00 from Thursday to Saturday, though individual counters set their own hours.

If you come, arrive around 11:30 to see the stalls before the lunch crowd, eat, and then walk five minutes along Rua Coelho da Rocha to the Casa Fernando Pessoa, or about 15 minutes to the Basílica da Estrela and the Jardim da Estrela, where the 28 also stops. Allow two and a half to three hours from the ship for the round trip and lunch. Skip it on a short call, or if you have not yet seen the Baixa, Alfama or Belém.
description.history: The market opened in 1934 to serve Campo de Ourique, a residential district laid out on a grid from the late 19th century on the western edge of the city. Like Lisbon's other municipal markets, it lost trade as supermarkets spread, and it was remodelled in 1991. A second remodelling in 2013 kept the traditional stalls around the edges and turned the central hall into food and drink counters with shared tables, one of the first Lisbon markets to combine the two. The market remains under Lisbon City Council, with the food hall run under a concession.
description.significance: It shows how a working municipal market has been kept alive by adding a food hall without pushing out the fishmongers, butchers and greengrocers. For a visitor its value is the setting: a residential district with few tourists, where lunch costs less than in the Baixa and you eat beside people doing their shopping. It is not a sight in itself.

directions.general: Located in Campo de Ourique residential neighborhood, west of central Lisbon between Estrela and Amoreiras
directions.fromCruisePort: About 4.2 km west, around an hour on foot. Tram 28 ends in Campo de Ourique (board at Sé, 13 minutes' walk from the terminal) or take a taxi (about 15 minutes).
directions.publicTransport: Tram 28 to Campo de Ourique area. Tram 25E from Cais do Sodré. Metro: Rato station (Yellow line) then 10-minute walk. Bus routes 702, 706, 720, 738, 773, 774.
directions.parking: Limited street parking in residential area. Some paid parking nearby.

seasonal.notes: Traditional stalls trade mainly in the morning; food counters set their own hours
Traditional stalls trade mainly in the morning; food counters set their own hours

closedDates: Individual stalls and counters may close on public holidays

admissionPrices.notes: Free entry. You pay per dish or drink at each counter; prices vary by stall.

visitingInformation.bestTimeToVisit: Late morning (about 11:30) to see the fresh-food stalls before the lunch rush.
visitingInformation.adviceForVisitors: Come in the morning for the traditional stalls and stay for an early lunch. Order at several counters and share a table. Combine with the Casa Fernando Pessoa or the Jardim da Estrela.

cruisePassengerInfo.accessibility: 4.2 km from the ship: taxi about 15 minutes, or tram 28 to the Campo de Ourique (Prazeres) terminus and a short walk. The market is on one level.
tips: Only worth the trip if you want a local lunch or are already riding tram 28; on a first, short visit, spend the time in the Baixa, Alfama or Belém instead.
Tram 28 ends at Campo de Ourique (Prazeres); it is slow and crowded in high season, so a taxi (about 15 minutes) is the quicker option.
The fresh-food stalls are best before midday; by mid-afternoon many have packed up.
The building opens at 07:00 every day and stays open until 23:00 Sunday to Wednesday and 01:00 Thursday to Saturday.
Order from several counters and share a table, as locals do.
The Casa Fernando Pessoa is on the same street, Rua Coelho da Rocha, a few minutes' walk away.
The Basílica and Jardim da Estrela are about 15 minutes' walk and on the tram 28 route back towards the centre.
Tinned fish and dried fruit from the stalls pack easily for the ship.

highlights: Traditional stalls for fish, meat, fruit and vegetables, bacalhau and bread
Charcuterie, tinned fish, spices, dried fruit and sweets
Central food hall with shared tables
Residential setting near the tram 28 terminus
Casa Fernando Pessoa a few minutes' walk along the same street
facilities: Shared seating in the central hall
Car park nearby on Rua Padre Francisco
Small services such as key cutting and shoe repair

accessibility.mobilityNotes: Single-level market hall. Aisles and seating get crowded at lunch and in the evening. The surrounding district is relatively flat for Lisbon.

languages: English at most food counters, less at the traditional stalls
